A homegrown catnip lotion has proven “just as effective as Deet” as a mosquito repellant in trials carried out in Uganda.

Shipment discovered at airport in Monrovia and valued at £14.2m had been falsely declared as seasoning cubes

Authorities in Liberia have charged five suspects over one of the largest drug seizures in the country’s history, after police found more than 200kg of cocaine falsely declared as Maggi seasoning cubes.

guardian.description:
Well-preserved fourth-century quarters reveal details of daily life, urban development and economic activities

Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a well-preserved Byzantine-era city in the western desert.

The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

El Obeid becomes key battleground in war between Sudan’s armed forces and their paramilitary enemies, the RSF

guardian.description:
TKMS beats South Korean rival to multibillion-dollar contract that will deepen Canada’s Nato ties

Canada has selected a German consortium to build a dozen cutting-edge submarines in one of the country’s largest-ever defence contracts that will further deepen its Nato ties before a crucial summit this week.

guardian.title: Cuban zoo celebrates birth of Bengal tigers amid energy crisis
guardian.description:
Arrival of endangered cats, including rare white cub, revitalises team straining under fuel and medicine shortages

For the Cuban zookeeper Ángel Cordero, the sight of four Bengal ⁠tiger cubs playing in a cage at the Cuban national zoo is a small miracle on an island stifled by shortages ⁠of fuel, medicine and ⁠days-long power outages.

The ​birth of these endangered big cats – including an exceedingly rare white tiger – has revitalised a team of zoo workers, he said.

guardian.title: Rodríguez defends Venezuela’s emergency earthquake response as number of bodies expected to soar
guardian.description:
Interim president says unrest will not break out despite anger at official response to the 24 June disaster

Venezuela’s interim president has defended her country’s emergency response to the twin earthquakes that have killed more than 3,000 people, vowing the country would not descend into social unrest.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger at what they see as the US-backed government’s inadequate response to the 24 June disaster before international teams arrived.

rfi.description: Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Wednesday that Greenland was "not for sale" following remarks by President Donald Trump suggesting the territory should be controlled by Washington and not Copenhagen.

rfi.description: Oil prices jumped more than three percent on Wednesday as the Middle East crisis burst back into the spotlight with US and Iranian forces exchanging strikes after attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, fuelling fresh supply fears.

rfi.title: Switzerland beat Colombia on penalties to set up last eight date with Argentina
rfi.description: Switzerland beat Colombia in a penalty shootout on Tuesday to advance to the last eight at the World Cup for the first time since 1954. They will play Argentina on Saturday in Kansas City.

rfi.title: TotalEnergies to discuss Syria offshore exploration, still wary of insecurity
rfi.description: TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanné said security concerns still rule out a return to onshore oil operations, but confirmed the French company is rebuilding its Iraq-Syria oil transit routes.

rfi.title: Le Pen confirms  presidential bid after Paris appeals court upholds conviction
rfi.description: The leader of France's far-right National Rally, Marine Le Pen, said on Tuesday she would run for president next year after an embezzlement conviction was confirmed on appeal, a ruling she said she would challenge before the country's highest court.

rfi.title: Climate justice in Africa: floods, fossil fuels and the fightback
rfi.description: This week in Spotlight on Africa, we look at climate change, environmental justice and the challenges of adaptation. While Europe's heatwaves make headlines, temperatures are also climbing across Africa, with parts of the Sahel approaching 50°C. West Africa is also experiencing severe flooding caused by climate change. Yet Africa is also a source of innovation and solutions, as we'll be discussing today.

rfi.title: Macron condemns Paraguayan senator's racist remarks as Mbappé hits back
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé condemned a Paraguayan senator on Monday for making racist comments about him following France's World Cup victory over Paraguay, calling her "despicable" and "not worthy" of her position.

rfi.title: Argentina return from the brink to beat Egypt and reach World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Argentina advanced to the last eight at the World Cup after recovering from a two-goal deficit to see off Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday.

rfi.title: EU warns France under-15 social media bill could breach European law
rfi.description: The European Commission has warned that a French bill that would ban children under the age of 15 from social media would infringe the European Union’s online content law by giving French regulators powers that go beyond the bloc’s legal framework.

rfi.title: NATO summit in Ankara tests unity as Ukraine war and Trump tensions loom
rfi.description: As NATO leaders gather in Ankara tomorrow, Tuesday, the alliance faces a stark test of unity, burden-sharing and strategic clarity, with the war in Ukraine, transatlantic tensions and Middle East instability all pressing heavily on the agenda.

rfi.title: De Ketelaere shines as Belgium trump US to advance to World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Charles de Ketelaere scored twice as Belgium swept past the United States 4-1 on Monday night to reach the last eight at the World Cup.

rfi.title: European football chiefs hit out at Fifa move to lift ban on US star Balgoun
rfi.description: European football's governing body Uefa on Monday lashed out at the decision of World Cup organisers Fifa to suspend the immediate one-match ban of the United States striker Folarin Balogun following the intervention of US President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: France's first diagnosed Ebola patient recovers after treatment
rfi.description: A French doctor who was the first-ever diagnosed case of Ebola in the country has made a full recovery and has been discharged from hospital.

rfi.title: Major wildfires burn in Southern France as early fire season hits Europe
rfi.description: Firefighters are fighting wildfires across southern France and other parts of Europe, and authorities are warning that this year’s fire season has started a month earlier than usual after early heatwaves in May and June left vegetation particularly dry and vulnerable.

rfi.title: Macron to become first Western European leader to visit post-Assad Syria
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron ​will visit ‌Syria to discuss ways to ​strengthen bilateral ​relations and issues of ⁠mutual interest, ​the Syrian presidency has announced, in what would be the first visit by a Western European head of state since Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

rfi.title: Merino's late strike takes Spain past Portugal into World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Mikel Merino scored in second half stoppage time at the Dallas Stadium on Monday to send Spain past Portugal into the last eight at the 2026 World Cup and end the World Cup career of Portugal skipper Cristiano Ronaldo.

rfi.title: Rebels seize key town of Anéfis as they tighten grip on northern Mali
rfi.description: Tuareg separatists and al-Qaeda affiliates appear to have secured control of a key town in northern Mali following a coordinated offensive by the rebels over the weekend. The Malian army and Russian mercenaries have been holed up in the key camp of Anéfis after the rebels launched their offensive on Saturday.

euronews.title: 43 ancient figurines discovered in Peru reveal secrets of the Americas’ oldest civilisation
euronews.description: Buried for nearly 4,000 years, 43 ancient figurines have been unearthed in Peru, revealing a rare glimpse into the rituals of the Caral civilisation - the oldest known civilisation in the Americas.

euronews.title: Trump attacks Spain calling it a 'wasted cause' and orders trade to stop
euronews.description: The US president had already threatened in March to take economic reprisals against Spain after Moncloa blocked the use of the Rota and Morón bases for Washington’s bombing campaign against Iran.

euronews.title: Oil spikes and European stock markets slide as Trump says Iran ceasefire over
euronews.description: Crude oil prices rose more than 6% to a two-week high after US President Donald Trump declared the interim accord to end the war with Iran "over", while fresh US military strikes renewed concerns about oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

euronews.title: Fake videos exploit Germany's East-West divide before key elections
euronews.description: Researchers say a coordinated influence campaign they suspect to be linked to Moscow is impersonating German media to exploit East-West divisions ahead of Germany's September state elections.

euronews.title: At least seven killed in fresh Russian strikes on Ukraine as NATO leaders meet in Turkey
euronews.description: Russia has hit the Ukrainian capital with several large deadly attacks over the last week, killing more than 50 this month in a spate of ballistic missile and drone strikes.

euronews.title: Spain pitches  €850bn per year in common EU borrowing
euronews.description: Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo will pitch a new common debt mechanism ahead of a meeting of euro-area finance ministers in Brussels on Thursday.

euronews.title: 'The Trump Curse': Is Donald Trump a bad omen for sports teams?
euronews.description: Following the elimination of the US at the World Cup, social media went into a frenzy with claims of a “Trump curse”. There seems to be prior form, as fans are citing other losses linked to Trump’s team endorsements or even his presence at games.

euronews.title: Got €200,000 to spare? This ultra-exclusive trip for the 2026 solar eclipse could be yours
euronews.description: Meliá Hotels International’s travel package to the Balearic Islands for August’s total solar eclipse is so exclusive that it's only available for one booking at each of its two hotels. The package includes flights on a private jet, a stay in a presidential suite, and a viewing experience at sea.

euronews.title: Erdogan gives world leaders a ceremonial welcome ahead of NATO summit
euronews.description: NATO leaders including Trump and Zelenskyy arrive in Ankara for a state dinner hosted by Erdogan ahead of key summit talks in Turkey.

euronews.title: More than 30,000 votes cast so far in search of South Korea’s top travel spots
euronews.description: South Korea has extended voting for its ambitious travel directory of the 10,000 must-visit destinations across the country. So far, more than 30,000 people have already had their say.

euronews.title: Who in Europe is the most affected by extreme heatwaves?
euronews.description: Europeans are experiencing another record-breaking heatwave, but not everyone is affected equally. Who is the most affected by these extreme climate events on the old continent?

euronews.title: Florence, Prague and Salzburg: These are the best cities in Europe, according to Travel + Leisure
euronews.description: After votes were cast by more than 200,000 people, San Miguel de Allende in Mexico came out on top on the overall world list, with the highest ranked European city coming out 13th.

euronews.title: NATO leaders to meet after Trump restates Greenland claim
euronews.description: Trump dashed hopes of a two-day summit by telling reporters the US should "control" Greenland. The Danish prime minister hit back, calling on the US to "respect Danish sovereignty".

euronews.title: 'Russian threat' moves to the Arctic, Canadian Foreign Minister warns
euronews.description: "The Russian threat is moving further and further north towards the Arctic Circle. We need to be prepared at all times across various domains", Canada's Foreign Affairs Minister, Anita Anand, said in an interview with Euronews, referring to the purchase of 12 submarines.

euronews.title: 'Greenland is not for sale' Denmark's Frederiksen reminds Trump
euronews.description: The renewed dispute comes months after Donald Trump revived his long-standing ambition for the United States to acquire Greenland, a proposal repeatedly rejected by Denmark and Greenland's leaders.

euronews.title: Celebrating Greece and its ancient gods: Annual polytheism festival takes place on Mount Olympus
euronews.description: Mount Olympus is a sight to behold each summer as torchlight processions, symbolic ceremonies and theatrical performances bring communities together in a shared celebration of ancient Greek mythology.

euronews.title: Le Pen 'will demonstrate innocence' despite embezzlement conviction, MEP Leggeri claims
euronews.description: Marine Le Pen ally Fabrice Leggeri claims the National Rally presidential candidate will prove her innocence despite an appeals court upholding her conviction for the misuse of millons in EU funds on Tuesday.

euronews.title: Watch: Fake condoms, counterfeit weight-loss pens and the toy labels testing EU borders
euronews.description: Anti-fraud investigators at OLAF just broke up an international smuggling group. Criminals tried to slip their illegal cargo past European border checks as children's toys to evade customs controls. But the boxes did not contain toys at all.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Marine Le Pen condamnée en appel : « Je me réjouis que Marine puisse porter nos couleurs », déclare Jordan Bardella, au lancement de la campagne du RN dans la Sarthe
lemonde.description: Marine Le Pen a été reconnue coupable en appel, mardi, dans le procès des assistants parlementaires européens du Front national. Elle a annoncé, dans la foulée, qu’elle serait tout de même candidate à l’élection présidentielle en 2027.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump affirme que le cessez-le-feu avec l’Iran est « terminé », après la reprise de frappes massives
lemonde.description: Les Etats-Unis ont annoncé, mardi, avoir bombardé plus de 80 cibles en Iran en riposte à des tirs iraniens sur des navires commerciaux dans le détroit d’Ormuz, déclenchant mercredi des représailles de Téhéran.

lemonde.title: L’appel des Prix Nobel pour la paix en Ukraine : « Cessez-le-feu ! Evacuez les morts et les blessés du champ de bataille ! »
lemonde.description: Dans une lettre adressée aux présidents ukrainien et russe, 44 lauréats du prix Nobel, emmenés par le cofondateur du journal russe « Novaïa Gazeta », Dmitri Mouratov, proposent un arrêt immédiat des hostilités, comme première étape vers la paix.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies : la préfecture de l’Hérault annule les feux d’artifice prévus du 10 au 16 juillet ; un incendie « contenu » dans le département a repris sa progression
lemonde.description: Le feu de Carlencas-et-Levas, qui était « contenu » après avoir parcouru 275 hectares depuis dimanche, a repris sa progression en raison d’un « changement de vent », ont fait savoir les pompiers. Seuls les feux d’artifice tirés en mer sont maintenus dans le département.

lemonde.title: « Les Groenlandais ont été très clairs : ils ne souhaitent pas faire partie des Etats-Unis », répond la première ministre danoise, Mette Frederiksen, à Donald Trump
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », la dirigeante danoise revient sur les déclarations de Donald Trump au sommet de l’OTAN, à Ankara, au sujet d’une prise de contrôle américaine de l’île, et sur l’autonomie stratégique européenne qu’elle appelle de ses vœux.

lemonde.title: « Une Coupe du monde n’est pas un miroir des relations internationales, ou alors un miroir déformant »
lemonde.description: Excepté la mise au ban de la Russie par les instances européennes et internationales depuis son agression de l’Ukraine en 2022, la géopolitique du football n’a pas grand-chose à voir avec la géopolitique tout court, même si la compétition est riche d’enseignements, relève Gilles Paris, éditorialiste au « Monde », dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: Sommet de l’OTAN : Donald Trump annonce que les Etats-Unis vont « cesser tout échange commercial » avec l’Espagne
lemonde.description: « Notre pays entretient d’excellentes relations sociales, culturelles et économiques avec les Etats-Unis, et nous n’avons aucunement l’intention que cela change », a réagi une source au sein de l’exécutif espagnol, disant accueillir ces déclarations « avec calme ».

lemonde.title: Sécurité sociale : la crainte d’un tour de vis pendant l’été
lemonde.description: Lors du comité d’alerte des finances publiques, le gouvernement a exprimé, mardi, l’intention de « refroidir » les dépenses de notre système de solidarité à hauteur de 1 milliard d’euros en 2026, sans préciser comment et à quel moment il comptait procéder.

lemonde.title: Procès de la loge maçonnique Athanor : des peines allant jusqu’à trente ans de prison ont été requises
lemonde.description: Des membres d’une loge maçonnique des Hauts-de-Seine sont accusés d’avoir commandité des contrats, allant de l’intimidation violente au meurtre. L’accusation a détaillé le fonctionnement de cette « PME du crime ».

lemonde.title: « Dry Leaf », éloge de la trajectoire imprévisible du ballon de foot… et de l’errance au cinéma
lemonde.description: Alexandre Koberidze, figure de la nouvelle vague géorgienne, livre un splendide film essai dans lequel un homme parcourt les stades, à la recherche de sa fille.

lemonde.title: Education nationale : nouvelle nette hausse du nombre de saisines de la médiatrice
lemonde.description: Les services de la médiatrice ont traité plus de 28 000 saisines, soit 22 % de plus qu’en 2024, et 60 % de plus qu’en 2020. Celle-ci met en garde contre le fonctionnement du système éducatif, dans de nombreux cas, qui peut « provoquer ou aggraver le mal-être des usagers ou des agents ».

lemonde.title: Sainte-Soline : la Défenseure des droits dénonce les manquements du maintien de l’ordre
lemonde.description: Dans sa décision publiée mercredi 8 juillet, Claire Hédon critique vivement la gestion par les autorités de la manifestation contre les mégabassines, le 25 mars 2023, qui a fait près de 250 blessés, principalement chez les manifestants, mais aussi chez les gendarmes. Elle déplore une « logique de confrontation ».

lemonde.title: Pluies diluviennes en Chine : au moins 17 morts, les secours mobilisés
lemonde.description: Au moins 130 000 personnes ont été évacuées à la suite des intempéries liées au typhon Maysak, selon les autorités locales. Les catastrophes naturelles frappent régulièrement la Chine, en particulier l’été.

lemonde.title: Scission de Vivendi : la cour d’appel donne gain de cause à Vincent Bolloré
lemonde.description: C’est la deuxième fois que la Cour se prononce sur ce dossier boursier, sa première décision d’avril 2025, en défaveur du milliardaire conservateur, ayant été annulée fin novembre par la Cour de cassation.

lemonde.title: La « justice climatique », grande oubliée des politiques d’adaptation aux canicules
lemonde.description: Au nom du respect des droits humains à la santé et à la vie, ONG et chercheurs réclament des politiques d’adaptation au réchauffement climatique qui priorisent les populations les plus vulnérables et les plus exposées.

lemonde.title: Entre salariés et patrons, le grand malentendu des stratégies d’entreprise : « Mon patron en start-up pouvait changer d’avis du jour au lendemain en fonction de ce qu’il lisait sur LinkedIn »
lemonde.description: La stratégie d’entreprise apparaît à de nombreux salariés comme un exercice opaque, déconnecté du terrain, voire instrumentalisé pour faire accepter des réorganisations.

zeit.title: Schuldenbremse: Wie viele Schulden sollen es sein?
zeit.description: Eine Kommission hat Vorschläge zur Reform der Schuldenbremse vorgelegt. Sie liegen der ZEIT exklusiv vor und zeigen: Ein strenger Sparkurs könnte der Wirtschaft schaden.

zeit.title: Sepp Blatter: »Ich bin froh, dass ich mit dieser Fifa-Führung nichts zu tun habe«
zeit.description: Sepp Blatter war als Fifa-Präsident in viele Skandale verwickelt. Was aber zwischen seinem Nachfolger Gianni Infantino und Donald Trump passiert, findet er inakzeptabel.

zeit.title: Übernahmeangebot : UniCredit nähert sich Mehrheit bei Commerzbank
zeit.description: Die italienische Großbank UniCredit hat sich 17,6 Prozent weitere Anteile an der Commerzbank gesichert. Die Bundesregierung lehnt eine Übernahme weiterhin vehement ab.

zeit.title: Bürokratieabbau: Kontrollrat stellt Fortschritte bei Bürokratieabbau fest
Gesundheit: Studie: Wo bis 2040 besonders viele Hausärzte fehlen könnten
Schock, Wut und Existenzangst: Nach Olympia-Aus: Nordische Kombination bangt um Zukunft
Kriminalität: Urne gestohlen - Polizei appelliert an Täter
Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Trump äußert sich auf Gipfel »sehr verärgert über die Nato«
zeit.description: Auf dem Nato-Gipfel wiederholt der US-Präsident seine Kritik am Bündnis. Spanien bezeichnet er als »schrecklichen Partner« und will die Handelsbeziehungen abbrechen.

zeit.title: Polizeieinsatz: Schusswaffen-Alarm in Bitterfeld – Polizei gibt Entwarnung
Forschung: IWH erhält Empfehlung für weitere Millionenförderung
Amphibien: Bund: Viele wichtige Gewässer für Frösche kaum gepflegt
Polizeibeauftragter: Polizeibeauftragter verzeichnet starke Zunahme an Eingaben
Grenzkontrollen: Polizeibeauftragter fordert Debatte über Grenzkontrollen
zeit.description: Die Zahl der unerlaubten Einreisen an den deutschen Grenzen sinkt. Der Bundespolizeibeauftragte will daher eine Debatte über die Zukunft der Kontrollen anstoßen.

zeit.title: Krankenkassen: Grünenabgeordneter reicht Eilantrag gegen Krankenkassen-Gesetz ein
zeit.description: Die Grünen verlangen eine Verschiebung der Abstimmung über das GKV-Gesetz und ziehen vor das Verfassungsgericht. Den Abgeordneten bleibe zu wenig Zeit für eine Prüfung.

zeit.title: Digital Markets Act: Apple scheitert vor EU-Gericht mit Klage gegen strengere Regeln
zeit.description: Das EU-Gericht hat die Einstufung Apples als digitaler Torwächter bestätigt und eine Klage des Konzerns zurückgewiesen. Apple muss sich somit an strengere Regeln halten.

france24fr.title: Un nouvel épisode caniculaire "sévère et durable" en France, journée à risque d'incendie
france24fr.description: "Un épisode caniculaire sévère et durable" se profile pour la France, annonce Météo-France. Les températures en hausse concernent désormais 67 départements en vigilance orange. Dans ce contexte, les autorités ont mis en garde contre les risques "très sévères" d'incendies.

france24fr.title: IA : l'Europe face à la guerre des modèles américains et chinois
france24fr.description: Alors que deux sommets consacrés à l'intelligence artificielle se tiennent cette semaine à Genève et à Paris, la rivalité entre Washington et Pékin s’intensifie. Les modèles chinois séduisent par leurs coûts plus faibles, mais posent aussi de nouvelles questions de souveraineté.

france24fr.title: En Libye, des archéologues s'engagent pour la sauvegarde du patrimoine classé à l'UNESCO
france24fr.description: En Libye, des vestiges antiques à Cyrène et Apollonia, classés au patrimoine mondial de l'UNESCO restent menacés deux ans après la tempête Daniel. Des archéologues s'efforcent de réparer les dégâts avec des moyens limités pour préserver l'un des plus remarquables paysages archéologiques d'Afrique du Nord.

france24fr.title: Obsèques de Khamenei : partisans du régime et opposition partagent des images créées par IA
france24fr.description: Alors que les obsèques du guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei – tué lors d'une frappe américano-israélienne le 28 février – ont actuellement lieu à Téhéran, de prétendues images de l’événement ont été diffusées à la fois par des internautes prorégime et par l’opposition. Mais ces images ont été générées par IA.

france24fr.title: France : Marine Le Pen candidate à la présidentielle malgré sa condamnation en appel
france24fr.description: Marine Le Pen, qui a joué son va-tout en décidant d'être candidate malgré sa condamnation en appel, lance mercredi sa campagne dans la Sarthe, faisant fi des critiques de ses adversaires et du risque que son pari judiciaire osé échoue.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela : un fast-food transformé en centre de soins
france24fr.description: Au Venezuela, quinze jours après les deux violents séismes, le bilan s’alourdit de jour en jour et s’élève désormais à 3 685 morts. Un chiffre sans doute bien en deçà de la réalité : le nombre de personnes disparues se compte par milliers, voire par dizaines de milliers. À La Guaira, au cœur de la zone sinistrée, un fast-food s’est mué en poste de soins improvisé, où des bénévoles soignent les corps comme les esprits. Reportage Pascale Mariani et Maxime Pluvinet.

france24fr.title: Irak : dernière étape des funérailles de Khamenei avant l'inhumation
france24fr.description: Le cercueil de l'ayatollah iranien Ali Khamenei fait une halte en Irak mercredi, pour des processions dans les villes de Najaf et Kerbala qui abritent les sanctuaires les plus sacrés de l'islam chiite, avant l'inhumation dans son pays d'origine.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis lancent des frappes massives contre l'Iran, qui riposte dans deux pays du Golfe
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont annoncé mardi le lancement d'une série de "frappes puissantes" contre l'Iran et le rétablissement de leurs sanctions économiques sur le pétrole iranien, affirmant répondre ainsi aux attaques qui ont visé des navires commerciaux dans le détroit d'Ormuz.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Trump dit être "en colère" contre l'Otan, au sujet de l'Iran et du Groenland
En direct : Trump dit être "en colère" contre l'Otan, au sujet de l'Iran et du Groenland
france24fr.description: Au second jour du sommet de l'Otan à Ankara, le président américain Donald Trump a fait part de son mécontentement envers l'Alliance atlantique au sujet de l'Iran et du Groenland. Le secrétaire général de l'Otan, Mark Rutte, a assuré pour sa part que les États-Unis restaient "pleinement engagés", tout en ajoutant qu'il y avait une "attente" américaine. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Condamnation de Marine Le Pen en appel: "Ni empêchée ni réhabilitée"
france24fr.description: À la Une de la presse, ce mercredi 8 juillet, les réactions, en France et à l'étranger, à la décision de Marine Le Pen d'être candidate à la présidentielle, malgré sa condamnation en appel. L'étonnante stratégie de Nigel Farage, le patron du parti d'extrême-droite Reform UK, qui a annoncé hier sa démission en tant que député… pour tenter d'être réélu. Et l'incroyable victoire de l'Argentine face à l'Egypte en huitièmes de finale du Mondial.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi Samsung se prend une claque boursière malgré des profits astronomiques
france24fr.description: Le géant sud-coréen Samsung a connu une chute en Bourse de près de 6 % alors même que ses profits augmentent de 1 800 %. Une étrange mésaventure boursière pour l’un des principaux fournisseurs de semi-conducteurs, essentiels pour faire tourner la machine de l'intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Argentine et Leo Messi miraculés contre l'Égypte
france24fr.description: Menée 2-0 avec 15 minutes à jouer, l'Argentine a renversé l'Égypte (3-2) en huitièmes de finale de la Coupe du monde. Les Argentins affronteront la Suisse en quarts de finale.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan s'alourdit à 3 685 morts, efforts pour rouvrir l'aéroport de Caracas
france24fr.description: Le bilan du double séisme du 24 juin au Venezuela continue de s'alourdir et s'élève désormais à 3 685 morts, ont annoncé mardi les autorités, qui cherchent par ailleurs à rouvrir l'aéroport international de Caracas aux vols commerciaux "dès que possible".

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis passent de nouveau à l'action contre l'Iran
france24fr.description: L'armée américaine a mené, mardi, une série de frappes contre les installations militaires iraniennes. "Washington affirme que les attaques (contre trois navires commerciaux dans le détroit d'Ormuz, imputées à l'Iran) constituent une violation du cessez-le-feu et défend une riposte relevant du droit de légitime défense", explique Matthieu Mabin, le correspondant de France 24 à Washington. De son côté, l'État major militaire américain parle de frappes "destinées à imposer un lourd bilan".

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine signe des accords sur les drones militaires avec plusieurs pays européens
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a annoncé mardi la signature d'accords de coopération en matière de drones militaires avec le Danemark, les Pays-Bas et l'Estonie. Il a ajouté se préparer à en conclure avec l'Allemagne, la Finlande, la Norvège et le Canada.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: La Suisse au bout de l'ennui contre la Colombie, L'Égypte qui frôle l'exploit contre l'Argentine, la polémique sur l'arbitre entre l'Albiceleste et les Pharons ... Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Facundo Tello, l'Argentin aux dix cartons rouges qui va arbitrer France - Maroc
france24fr.description: L'Argentin Facundo Tello a été désigné, mardi, arbitre du quart de finale entre la France et le Maroc à la Coupe du monde 2026. À 44 ans, l'homme en noir sud-américain participe au deuxième Mondial de sa carrière après avoir déjà officié au Qatar, en 2022. Dans son pays, il s'est rendu célèbre en distribuant... dix cartons rouges en un seul match. Portrait.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Treffen zwischen Trump und Selenski geplant +++ Erdogan inszeniert Trumps Teilnahme am Nato-Gipfel mit Pomp
nzz.description: Die Verteidigungsallianz hat turbulente Monate hinter sich. In Ankara steht ein entscheidendes Treffen an. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Von «Gott mischt sich nicht in den Fussball ein» bis «Was für ein schlechtes Fussballspiel!» – das denkt die Welt über den Viertelfinaleinzug der Schweiz
nzz.description: Die Medien nennen das Spiel gegen Kolumbien zäh bis grauenhaft. Entsprechend gelassen blickt man in Argentinien auf den Viertelfinal gegen die Schweiz.

nzz.title: Wegen wiederholter Pannen: Swiss will gegen Flugsicherung Skyguide vorgehen
nzz.description: Dieses Jahr musste Skyguide wegen Softwareproblemen drei Mal den Flugverkehr einschränken. Nun prüft die Swiss eine Forderung nach Schadenersatz – gestützt auf ein Gerichtsurteil der EU.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das Nationalteam schafft den grössten Erfolg in der Fussballgeschichte der Schweiz – und lässt das Land träumen
nzz.description: Resilienz, Hartnäckigkeit und Gemeinsinn: Die Schweizer Nationalmannschaft erreicht in Vancouver Historisches – und kreiert mit der Viertelfinalqualifikation Bilder, die bleiben werden.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump erklärt Waffenruhe mit Iran für hinfällig +++ Ölpreise ziehen deutlich an
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar vereinbarten die beiden Länder Mitte Juni eine Waffenruhe. Doch diese ist fragil. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Unicredit nähert sich Mehrheit bei Commerzbank +++ Apple verliert vor dem EU-Gericht
BILDSTRECKE - Das Nato-Treffen in der Türkei in Bildern
nzz.description: Diese Woche treffen sich die Nato-Mitglieder zu ihrem 36. Gipfel, das zweite Mal in der Türkei. US-Präsident Donald Trump und der ukrainische Präsident Wolodimir Selenski sind ebenfalls angereist.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Spritpreise steigen nach Ende des Tankrabatts deutlich – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Zwei russische Raffinerien brennen nach Drohnenangriffen +++ Erneut russischer Angriff mit ballistischen Raketen auf Kiew
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Bereits mehr als 500 Ebola-Tote in Kongo-Kinshasa
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation WHO hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Es werden weitere Infizierte erwartet. Die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebolavirus.

nzz.title: Für Reiche ist Zürich die zweitteuerste Stadt der Welt – zum Glück kommen sie trotzdem. Die Restschweiz dankt
nzz.description: Nicht ganz ernst gemeinte Würdigung einer neuen Weltrangliste für Wohlhabende auf Wohnungssuche.

nzz.title: Das Schweizer Nationalteam spielt die beste WM seiner Geschichte – weil es auf alle Eventualitäten eine Antwort findet
nzz.description: Yakins Team trotzt sämtlichen Widerständen und zieht in den WM-Viertelfinal ein. Die Spielergeneration um Granit Xhaka und Ricardo Rodríguez hat eine Beharrlichkeit entwickelt wie keine vor ihr.

nzz.title: «It's over»: Trump erklärt den Waffenstillstand mit Iran für beendet
nzz.description: Die Eskalationsspirale am Persischen Golf droht erneut in Gang zu kommen. Nach Angriffen auf Tanker sagt Washington, Iran habe die Rahmenvereinbarung gebrochen. Das amerikanische Militär greift an, Sanktionen auf iranisches Öl treten wieder in Kraft.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Fragwürdige Liebschaften, richterliche Fehden, und alle schauen weg: Kann man die Justiz sich selber überlassen?
nzz.description: Die Politik will den Richtern ein Aufpassergremium zur Seite stellen, die Richter wollen im Gegenzug fest bis zur Pensionierung oder gar auf Lebenszeit im Amt bleiben. Bloss das nicht!

nzz.title: KI für Gesundheitsfragen: wieso die Schweizer gegenüber Dr. Chat-GPT so skeptisch sind
nzz.description: Fast die Hälfte der Schweizer scheut sich bei gesundheitlichen Problemen, KI zu konsultieren. Ein Mediziner findet aber, dass KI den Arztbesuch in vielen Fällen durchaus sinnvoll ergänzen könnte.

observador.title: Avião desaparece no Paquistão com cinco pessoas a bordo
observador.description: O Boeing 737  perdeu o contacto com o controlo aéreo na terça-feira à noite quando se aproximava de Karachi depois de descidas acentuadas Dados de radar indicam que a aeronave poderá ter caído no mar.

observador.title: As imagens do regresso da seleção a Portugal
observador.description: Dezenas de adeptos madrugaram para receber a seleção nacional no Aeroporto Humberto Delgado. Roberto Martínez chegou sorridente e Ronaldo foi o grande ausente.

observador.title: Estado terá perdido 460 milhões com fraude nos combustíveis
observador.description: Fuga aos impostos nos combustíveis importados de Espanha tem vindo a crescer todos os anos. Estudo indica que Estado perdeu 460 milhões só em 2025. Há medidas para travar fraude, mas ainda demoram.

observador.title: Bobb, o norueguês que cresceu no Porto
observador.description: Viveu no Porto e tentou jogar nos azuis e brancos, mas a FIFA travou o processo e acabou por regressar à Noruega. Depois chegou ao City, a tempo de vencer uma Premier, antes de ir para o Fulham.

observador.title: "Não deixem pedra sobre pedra nos abusos da Igreja"
observador.description: Rute Agulhas, psicóloga, defende o rigor dos protocolos nas audições de vítimas. Alerta também para a falta de psicólogos e de respostas no Serviço Nacional de Saúde.

observador.title: "É necessário que haja mais hospitais privados"
observador.description: A análise aos números da Entidade Reguladora da Saúde que aponta para um aumento de 59% da despesa directa dos portugueses com hospitais privados é de Óscar Gaspar. Escutamos também Pedro Pita Barros.

observador.title: 10h. Donald Trump anuncia fim do cessar-fogo no Irão
observador.description: Declarações na cimeira da NATO depois da troca de ataques desta noite. Ainda neste jornal, Associação Portuguesa de Hospitalização Privada pede mais unidades de saúde privadas no país.

observador.title: Vale a pena investir em Certificados do Tesouro?
observador.description: Os recuperados Certificados do Tesouro devem ser comparados com os Certificados de Aforro e com os depósitos bancários. Todos têm características e rentabilidades diferentes.

observador.title: Há jogadores sobressalentes ou isso é só para os pneus?
observador.description: O Marco Neves desfaz mitos políticos sobre as cores, explica por que não há atletas "sobressalentes" e viaja até ao Brasil para revelar as diferenças entre o calão e o "baixo calão".

observador.title: Genéricos: mais saúde para todos, mais valor para o país
observador.description: Os medicamentos genéricos garantem maior acesso a tratamentos a um custo menor, beneficiando utentes e o país. Luís Abrantes, CEO da Generis, explica o impacto deste tipo de medicamentos.

observador.title: Nova peça de Tiago Rodrigues chega a Portugal em setembro
observador.description: Espetáculo de dois atores imagina um universo em que os habitantes da Terra vivem em condições precárias devido ao aquecimento global. Sobe ao palco da Culturgest, em Lisboa, de 10 a 20 de setembro.

observador.title: Emídio Sousa visita Caracas para reforçar apoio de Portugal
observador.description: Após Portugal ter enviado toneladas de ajuda humanitária, o Secretário de Estado das Comunidades Portuguesas visita o país para reforçar a solidariedade com os mais afetados.

observador.title: 2 anos de Endless: caso de sucesso de Retail Media
observador.description: A Endless, a plataforma de Retail Media da MC, celebrou o seu segundo aniversário na Estufa by Tazte Secret Spot, em Monsanto, reunindo marcas, agências e parceiros.

observador.title: Queixas contra PSP e GNR aumentam cerca de 60% em seis anos
observador.description: A IGAI instaurou sete processos de contraordenação, 46 disciplinares e 29 de natureza inspetiva. Os agentes da PSP foram os mais visados, num total de 1.722 queixas realizadas o ano passado.

observador.title: Fernando Alexandre: será este o fim da estrela da educação?
observador.description: O ministro da Educação tenta gerir o caos dos exames enquanto o Tribunal Constitucional mima agressores domésticos. Já a UE quer travar as taxas das companhias low-cost.

observador.title: 9h. Cimeira NATO. Luís Montenegro deixa aviso aos Aliados
observador.description: O chefe do Governo espera que os interesses nacionais sejam assegurados pelos restantes países da organização. Ainda, moradores de Almada promovem um cordão humano. E as declarações de Mark Rutte.

observador.title: Montenegro no país das maravilhas: futebol ou política?
observador.description: Montenegro vê "glória" no relvado com Portugal em alerta vermelho com os incêndios. Quaresma critica a falta de garra e Ronaldo divide: orgulho luso ou embaixador saudita?

observador.title: O autocarro que matou em Sintra e a falta de água em Almada
observador.description: Duas pessoas morreram e mais de 25 ficaram feridas num incidente com um autocarro em Sintra. Falta água em Almada e vai continuar a faltar. André Ventura tenta travar guerras internas no Chega.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Thiersee mahnt nach mutmaßlicher Bären-Sichtung zu Vorsicht
spiegel.description: Das Tier soll sich auf die Hinterbeine gestellt haben: Zwei Landwirte haben in Österreich offenbar einen Bären entdeckt. Die Gemeinde reagiert.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: 50 Millionen Euro für bessere Kundeninfos
spiegel.description: Mit neuer IT und einer KI-Assistentin will die Deutsche Bahn Reisende schneller und verlässlicher informieren. Auch kurzfristige Gleiswechsel sollen künftig früher angezeigt werden.

spiegel.title: Braunschweig: Familie findet kistenweise Knochen im Garten – sie stammen von Menschen
spiegel.description: Eine Familie will ihren Garten verschönern – und entdeckt dabei Dutzende Knochen. Gerichtsmediziner stellen fest: Es sind Menschenknochen.

spiegel.title: Mannheim: Polizist soll mutmaßliche Opfer von Zwangsprostitution vergewaltigt haben
spiegel.description: Die Staatsanwaltschaft Mannheim hat Anklage erhoben: Einem Polizisten wird vorgeworfen, zwei Frauen vergewaltigt zu haben. Der Beamte soll sich dabei die Notsituation der mutmaßlichen Opfer zunutze gemacht haben.

spiegel.title: Apple gegen EU-Kommission: iPhone-Konzern scheitert mit Klage
spiegel.description: Die EU sieht den US-Konzern als sogenannten Torwächter und will ihm besonders strenge Regeln machen. Apple versucht, das zu verhindern. Bislang ohne Erfolg.

spiegel.title: »Magnifica Humanitas« von Papst Leo XIV.: Buch über KI sollte zur Pflichtlektüre werden – Kolumne
spiegel.description: Die 245 Weisheiten von Leo XIV. über die Herausforderungen durch künstliche Intelligenz sind Pflichtlektüre für Parteien, die programmatisch gerade auf dem Schlauch stehen. Und sie lesen sich sogar gut.

spiegel.title: Zendaya: Tom Holland überbrachte ihr die Nachricht ihrer Rolle in »Die Odyssee«
spiegel.description: Einen Tag nach ihrem Partner bekam auch Zendaya ein Angebot von Regisseur Christopher Nolan. Die Nachricht durfte Tom Holland selbst überbringen: »Ich war total begeistert.«

spiegel.title: Smart Glasses: Meta kündigt zusätzliche Sicherheitsvorkehrungen für Kamera-Brillen an
spiegel.description: Mit sogenannten Smart Glasses will der Instagram-Konzern Meta Kameras und KI-Funktionen noch stärker in den Alltag integrieren. Nach mehreren Berichten über Spanner-Aufnahmen verspricht er nun kleinlaut Nachbesserungen.

spiegel.title: Salzburg: Kulturschaffende wollen Stefan-Zweig-Villa der Öffentlichkeit zugänglich machen
spiegel.description: Im Paschinger Schlössl in Salzburg empfing der Schriftsteller Stefan Zweig einst Kollegen wie Thomas Mann. Mittlerweile gehört das Anwesen Wolfgang Porsche, er will es verkaufen. Nun fordern Künstler den Staat zum Eingreifen auf.

spiegel.title: Gesundheitsreform: Geplante Neuregelung könnte Druck auf Langzeitpatienten erhöhen
spiegel.description: 21,6 Milliarden Euro kostet das Krankengeld die Kassen – weshalb nun bei den Langzeitpatienten gespart werden soll. Expertinnen berichten, wie diese Gruppe jetzt schon drangsaliert und wie sehr das Problem vergrößert wird.

spiegel.title: Louise Lasser ist tot: Star aus »Mary Hartman, Mary Hartman«
spiegel.description: Als neurotische Hausfrau Mary Hartman erlangte Louise Lasser Bekanntheit. Später spielte die Ex-Frau von Woody Allen in »Requiem for a Dream« und der Serie »Girls« mit. Nun ist die US-Schauspielerin im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: Pamplona: Verletzte auch bei zweiter Stierhatz bei »Sanfermines«
spiegel.description: Im spanischen Pamplona jagen sich mal wieder Stiere und Menschen durch die Straßen. Auch beim zweiten Lauf wurden Menschen verletzt. Tierschutzgruppen demonstrieren gegen die umstrittene Tradition.

spiegel.title: Bildung: Jede dritte Lehrkraft in Deutschland ist 50 Jahre oder älter
spiegel.description: Relativ alt, viel Teilzeit, viele Frauen und immer mehr Quereinsteiger: Zu diesen Erkenntnissen über die Lehrkräfte in Deutschland kommt das Statistische Bundesamt. Es gibt deutliche regionale Unterschiede.

spiegel.title: Commerzbank: UniCredit baut Anteile bei Commerzbank weiter aus
spiegel.description: Nach einem Übernahmeangebot kontrollieren die Italiener nun 44 Prozent der Aktien. Eine Mehrheit erscheint zunehmend realistisch. In Frankfurt zeigt man sich dialogbereit, aber kämpferisch.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump will jeglichen Handel mit Spanien einstellen - Ärger wegen Irankrieg

phys-org.title: Hotter, drier weather could double water bills in some US cities, study finds
phys-org.description: Hotter, drier weather threatens to double water bills by midcentury in some cities, according to a Stanford-led study. The research, published in Nature Sustainability, is the first to comprehensively model how climate change, infrastructure investment and household water demand can combine to compound an already growing affordability crisis.

phys-org.title: Sensors, early starts: How Spain keeps working when heat hits
phys-org.description: The morning sun beats down on Antonio Reina as he tends a public garden in Barcelona, but he works reassured that a simple wristband protects him in the summer heat.

phys-org.title: Cambodia wants to bring tigers back, but should it?
phys-org.description: Pan Sok still remembers his relative screaming as a tiger dragged him away one night, deep inside the Cambodian rainforest where they were tapping trees for resin.

phys-org.title: What to know about the total solar eclipse due in August
phys-org.description: Day will briefly turn into night across a swath of northern Spain on Aug. 12, when the moon will completely cover the sun during a rare total solar eclipse.

phys-org.title: UK museums at 'sharp end' of climate change challenge
phys-org.description: As visitors peered at skeletons and preserved animals in a London zoological museum during a UK heat wave, staff focused on a different attraction: a computer screen glowing with red and green temperature indicators.

phys-org.title: 'Unique event': Solar eclipse fever fills empty Spain
phys-org.description: As a child, Enrique Bordallo would gaze in awe at the starry night sky in rural Spain. Next month's solar eclipse has now made his passion a popular obsession.

phys-org.title: How foreign direct investments affect employment and income in rural areas of the US
phys-org.description: Federal trade and industrial policies have triggered a new wave of foreign direct investment (FDI) in the United States, with some companies committing billions of dollars to U.S.-based manufacturing. Now, an analysis in Contemporary Economic Policy has found that FDI raises employment but has no significant effect on income in rural U.S. counties.

phys-org.title: How climate change affects interactions between owls and their prey
phys-org.description: A study published in Ecography has assessed how climate change may be destabilizing interactions between predators and prey in the wild—specifically, how owl–prey interactions have responded to environmental variability and resource availability over 24 years in the semi-arid ecosystem of Bosque Fray Jorge National Park in Chile.

phys-org.title: Global warming, increasing wildfire risk threaten viability of some California winery regions
phys-org.description: The U.S. is the fourth-largest wine-producing country by output volume, and approximately 80% of its production occurs in California. Ever since the 19th century, California's premier wine-growing regions have been the Napa Valley and Sonoma County, thanks to their favorable microclimate. But grape yield and quality are very sensitive to the local environment, which means the climate crisis could shake up California's wine industry.

phys-org.title: How tall and short trees can coexist in old growth forests
phys-org.description: Forests are shaped by light competition. The trees that grow the tallest have access to the most sunlight, blocking the rays and rendering the shaded space around them inhospitable to shorter trees below. In this stem exclusion phase of forest succession, the shorter trees often die. phys-org.title: Sponsorship is key to career progression but less than one in four relationships work
phys-org.description: A research report launched today reveals that sponsorship is a critical part of progression into senior leadership roles because it teaches individuals how advancement actually works in practice. But only a small proportion of sponsorship relationships—less than a quarter—are characterized by the mutual trust, candid feedback and active advocacy that really boost leaders' careers.

phys-org.title: How rocket launches could threaten Australia's coastal wildlife
phys-org.description: Space and rockets have been big news of late, from the successful Artemis 2 mission in April to the recent listing of SpaceX on the Nasdaq stock exchange.

phys-org.title: Migratory birds may carry fewer parasites between islands than expected, DNA shows
phys-org.description: A new study published in the Journal of Helminthology by researchers from the Estonian University of Life Sciences and the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, together with collaborators from Greenland and the Faroe Islands, has revealed surprisingly limited dispersal of Diplostomum parasites across North Atlantic islands. The findings challenge the common assumption that migratory birds readily transport parasites over large geographic distances.

phys-org.title: Quantum vacuum could help break molecular bonds with less energy, simulations suggest
phys-org.description: A team of researchers led by Felipe Herrera, a professor at the University of Santiago and a researcher at the Millennium Institute for Research in Optics (MIRO), has identified a quantum phenomenon that enables chemical bonds to be broken using significantly less energy than is normally required.

phys-org.title: Opportunities across childhood best predict degrees, earnings for low-income youth
phys-org.description: A new study led by a Boston College researcher has found that experiencing educational opportunities in all stages of childhood and adolescence is the best predictor of higher educational attainment and earnings for disadvantaged American youth, as opposed to the impact of learning access during any single phase.

phys-org.title: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft wakes from its longest hibernation in good health
phys-org.description: Following its longest hibernation period ever of nearly a year, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft has emerged in good health and is ready to begin transmitting science data gathered in the distant Kuiper Belt far beyond Pluto.

phys-org.title: Island life changed how Brazil's Noronha skink reproduces, but the lizard's strategy might be failing
phys-org.description: Visitors to the Fernando de Noronha archipelago, located about 340 miles (545 kilometers) off the coast of Pernambuco in northeastern Brazil, soon notice a small lizard. Seemingly ubiquitous, it roams among rocks, trails and urbanized areas, approaching people and stealing food in plain sight when it can, and rarely flees.

phys-org.title: Black women academics in my study said their main allies were white men: What this reveals
phys-org.description: Universities have a role in challenging the status quo on issues such as gender, race, nationality and sexuality. But all too often, they replicate societal inequalities.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, then, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.

proj-syn.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
proj-syn.description: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.

proj-syn.title: Just Say No to Remote Work
proj-syn.description: Even during the immediate post-pandemic period, when evidence on the labor-market effects of remote work was scant, there was a strong case to be made for going into the office, especially for younger workers. And now, multiple new studies have vindicated this intuition.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.

proj-syn.title: The Putin Escalation Risk
proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. The temptation to escape his predicament through a game-changing attack will grow stronger.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s New German Question
